quests.hint: Got something you earned — in this case, a higher position at work.
quests.explanation: 'Received a promotion and moved to a new office' is a natural career achievement phrase. 'Receive a promotion' is the standard collocation — 'get a promotion' is more informal but equally common.
quests.textToSpeak: She received a promotion and moved to a new office.
quests.textWithBlanks: She ___ a promotion and moved to a new office.

quests.hint: People who give their time and work without being paid.
quests.explanation: 'Volunteers cleaned up the beach last weekend' describes community action. 'Volunteer' can be a noun or a verb. 'Clean up' is a phrasal verb meaning to remove dirt or waste — commonly used for environmental activities.
quests.textToSpeak: The volunteers cleaned up the beach last weekend.
quests.textWithBlanks: The ___ cleaned up the beach last weekend.

quests.hint: Harm or destruction caused to something — it can be serious or minor.
quests.explanation: 'The storm caused serious damage to buildings' is a natural disaster-reporting phrase. 'Damage' is uncountable in English — you say 'serious damage,' not 'serious damages.' 'Caused damage' is the standard verb-noun combination.
quests.textToSpeak: The storm caused serious damage to several buildings in the area.
quests.textWithBlanks: The storm caused serious ___ to several buildings in the area.

quests.hint: Officially signed up or registered for a course or program.
quests.explanation: 'Enrolled in an online course to improve her skills' is natural professional development vocabulary. 'Enroll in' (American) / 'enrol in' (British) means to officially register. 'To improve her skills' states the purpose clearly.
quests.textToSpeak: She enrolled in an online course to improve her skills.
quests.textWithBlanks: She ___ in an online course to improve her skills.

quests.hint: A planned public activity or occasion that attracts many visitors.
quests.explanation: 'The event attracted thousands of visitors' is a very natural tourism or public affairs sentence. 'Attract visitors' is a common collocation — 'draw visitors' also works. 'From across the country' shows the event had wide national appeal.
quests.textToSpeak: The event attracted thousands of visitors from across the country.
quests.textWithBlanks: The ___ attracted thousands of visitors from across the country.

quests.hint: Feeling anxious or uneasy, especially before something important.
quests.explanation: 'Felt nervous before delivering his speech' is a very relatable experience. 'Nervous' is the most common word for pre-performance anxiety. 'In front of the crowd' adds the social pressure element that causes nervousness.
quests.textToSpeak: He felt nervous before delivering his speech in front of the crowd.
quests.textWithBlanks: He felt ___ before delivering his speech in front of the crowd.

quests.hint: Officially introduced something new to the public for the first time.
quests.explanation: 'Launched a new product at the annual conference' is a key business expression. 'Launch' (not 'start' or 'open') is the standard verb for new products, websites, or campaigns. 'Annual conference' means a yearly gathering.
quests.textToSpeak: The company launched a new product at the annual conference.
quests.textWithBlanks: The company ___ a new product at the annual conference.

quests.hint: Added things to a space to make it look more attractive or personal.
quests.explanation: 'Decorated her apartment with plants and paintings' means she added items to improve the look of her home. 'Decorate' implies making a space more beautiful or personal — more than just 'tidying.'
quests.textToSpeak: She decorated her apartment with colorful plants and paintings.
quests.textWithBlanks: She ___ her apartment with colorful plants and paintings.

quests.hint: Put money into something hoping it will grow or produce a return.
quests.explanation: 'Invested his savings in a small business' is common financial vocabulary. 'Invest in' (not 'put into') is the standard business English phrase. 'Savings' refers to money set aside over time — it is often used in the plural.
quests.textToSpeak: He invested his savings in a small business downtown.
quests.textWithBlanks: He ___ his savings in a small business downtown.

quests.hint: A prediction about what will happen — especially for the weather.
quests.explanation: 'The forecast says it will rain heavily this afternoon' is a natural way to report a weather prediction. 'Forecast' is the standard word for weather predictions. 'Heavy rain' is a fixed collocation — you never say 'big rain.'
quests.textToSpeak: The forecast says it will rain heavily this afternoon.
quests.textWithBlanks: The ___ says it will rain heavily this afternoon.

quests.hint: Said something briefly and casually, without going into much detail.
quests.explanation: 'Mentioned that he would be out of the office' implies the information was given as a passing remark. 'Mention' is softer than 'say' or 'announce' — it implies a brief, informal reference to something.
quests.textToSpeak: He mentioned that he would be out of the office next week.
quests.textWithBlanks: He ___ that he would be out of the office next week.

quests.hint: Showing certainty and self-assurance about what you are doing or saying.
quests.explanation: 'A confident answer during a job interview' describes how a candidate came across. 'Confident' is an important adjective for describing performance in professional situations. Interviewers always look for confident candidates.
quests.textToSpeak: The candidate gave a confident answer during the job interview.
quests.textWithBlanks: The candidate gave a ___ answer during the job interview.

quests.hint: Works without payment to help an organization or community.
quests.explanation: 'Volunteers at the local library every Saturday morning' — here 'volunteer' is used as a verb meaning to give one's time for free. 'Volunteer at + location' is a natural phrase for describing regular unpaid community work.
quests.textToSpeak: She volunteers at the local library every Saturday morning.
quests.textWithBlanks: She ___ at the local library every Saturday morning.

quests.hint: Made something publicly known for the first time — an official statement.
quests.explanation: 'The government announced new measures to protect the environment' is a very natural political news phrase. 'Announce' is used for official public declarations — more formal than 'say' and implying a prepared statement.
quests.textToSpeak: The government announced new measures to protect the environment.
quests.textWithBlanks: The government ___ new measures to protect the environment.

quests.hint: An official document needed to cross international borders.
quests.explanation: 'Realized he had left his passport at the hotel' is a very common travel panic scenario. 'Left' here means 'forgotten and left behind' — not 'departed.' Without a passport, international travel is impossible.
quests.textToSpeak: He realized he had left his passport at the hotel.
quests.textWithBlanks: He realized he had left his ___ at the hotel.

quests.hint: Gave someone the confidence or motivation to do something.
quests.explanation: 'Encouraged the students to ask questions freely' is a positive teaching behavior. 'Encourage + someone + to + verb' is an important grammatical pattern in English, commonly used in educational and professional contexts.
quests.textToSpeak: The teacher encouraged the students to ask questions freely.
quests.textWithBlanks: The teacher ___ the students to ask questions freely.

quests.hint: An error or something done incorrectly — we all make them sometimes.
quests.explanation: 'Noticed a mistake and corrected it immediately' shows careful professional behavior. 'Mistake' is the most common word for an error. The paired verbs 'noticed' and 'corrected' show a responsible sequence of actions.
quests.textToSpeak: She noticed a mistake in the report and corrected it immediately.
quests.textWithBlanks: She noticed a ___ in the report and corrected it immediately.

quests.hint: Able to be adjusted or changed to suit different needs or schedules.
quests.explanation: 'Flexible working hours' is a very common modern workplace benefit. 'Flexible' means the schedule can be adapted. This phrase appears frequently in job advertisements and workplace discussions.
quests.textToSpeak: The company offers flexible working hours for its employees.
quests.textWithBlanks: The company offers ___ working hours for its employees.

quests.hint: To focus your full mental attention on something you are doing.
quests.explanation: 'Struggled to concentrate because the office was noisy' is a very relatable workplace challenge. 'Concentrate' means giving full mental attention — a synonym is 'focus.' 'Because' introduces the reason for the difficulty.
quests.textToSpeak: He struggled to concentrate because the office was noisy.
quests.textWithBlanks: He struggled to ___ because the office was noisy.

quests.hint: Refused or declined something that was offered to you — a two-word phrasal verb.
quests.explanation: 'Turned down the job offer because the salary was too low' uses the phrasal verb 'turn down,' meaning to refuse. This is very common in professional English. The reason 'salary was too low' explains the decision.
quests.textToSpeak: She turned down the job offer because the salary was too low.
quests.textWithBlanks: She ___ down the job offer because the salary was too low.

quests.hint: Very old — belonging to a civilization thousands of years ago.
quests.explanation: 'Ancient artifacts from Egypt' — 'ancient' is the correct word for things thousands of years old. 'Antique' is used for objects a few hundred years old; 'ancient' implies a much older, historical civilization.
quests.textToSpeak: The museum has a collection of ancient artifacts from Egypt.
quests.textWithBlanks: The museum has a collection of ___ artifacts from Egypt.

quests.hint: A Romance language widely spoken in Spain and Latin America.
quests.explanation: 'Has been learning Spanish for three years' uses the present perfect continuous — showing an ongoing activity that started in the past. This tense is very common in spoken English when describing long-term activities.
quests.textToSpeak: She has been learning Spanish for three years and speaks it quite well.
quests.textWithBlanks: She has been learning ___ for three years and speaks it quite well.

quests.hint: Expressed dissatisfaction or unhappiness about a product or service.
quests.explanation: 'The customer complained that the product was damaged during shipping' is a natural customer service scenario. 'Complain + that + clause' is the standard grammar pattern. 'During shipping' tells us the damage happened in transit.
quests.textToSpeak: The customer complained that the product was damaged during shipping.
quests.textWithBlanks: The customer ___ that the product was damaged during shipping.

quests.hint: Copied digital content from the internet onto your device.
quests.explanation: 'Downloaded the app and created an account within minutes' is essential modern technology vocabulary. 'Download' means to copy from a server to your device — the opposite of 'upload.' 'Within minutes' shows how quick the process was.
quests.textToSpeak: He downloaded the app and created an account within minutes.
quests.textWithBlanks: He ___ the app and created an account within minutes.

quests.hint: A resource that runs out when you don't finish something quickly enough.
quests.explanation: 'Ran out of time and couldn't finish the test' — 'run out of' is a phrasal verb meaning a supply has been used up completely. 'Ran out of time' is one of the most commonly heard phrases in exam and work contexts.
quests.textToSpeak: She ran out of time and couldn't finish the last section of the test.
quests.textWithBlanks: She ran out of ___ and couldn't finish the last section of the test.

quests.hint: Large and important enough to be noticed and to make a real difference.
quests.explanation: 'A significant improvement compared to last year' is standard business reporting language. 'Significant' means meaningfully large — stronger than 'slight' or 'small,' and more measured than 'huge.' Used widely in formal reports.
quests.textToSpeak: The sales figures showed a significant improvement compared to last year.
quests.textWithBlanks: The sales figures showed a ___ improvement compared to last year.

quests.hint: Vehicles moving on roads — there can be a great deal of it at busy times.
quests.explanation: 'Arrived on time despite the heavy traffic' shows persistence against difficulty. 'Despite' introduces a contrast: he arrived on time even though traffic was bad. 'Heavy' is always the adjective used with 'traffic.'
quests.textToSpeak: He managed to arrive on time despite the heavy traffic.
quests.textWithBlanks: He managed to arrive on time despite the heavy ___.

quests.hint: Made available to the public in written or digital form.
quests.explanation: 'Published their findings in a scientific journal' is standard academic English. 'Publish' is the specific verb for making written research available. A 'journal' in academic contexts is a regular publication containing research articles.
quests.textToSpeak: The research team published their findings in a scientific journal.
quests.textWithBlanks: The research team ___ their findings in a scientific journal.

quests.hint: Having too much to handle at once — feeling buried under pressure.
quests.explanation: 'Felt overwhelmed by the amount of work' describes a common emotional experience under pressure. 'Overwhelmed by' is a natural word combination. This is an important word for describing stress in academic and professional settings.
quests.textToSpeak: She felt overwhelmed by the amount of work she had to do.
quests.textWithBlanks: She felt ___ by the amount of work she had to do.

quests.hint: A formal legal agreement signed by two or more parties.
quests.explanation: 'The contract was signed by both parties at the end of the meeting' uses the passive voice — very common in formal and legal English. 'Both parties' means the two sides involved. Signing at the end shows the conclusion of negotiations.
quests.textToSpeak: The contract was signed by both parties at the end of the meeting.
quests.textWithBlanks: The ___ was signed by both parties at the end of the meeting.
